decisions.reason: Footer codes are a separate behavior and the same source message already has a complete candidate MODIFY establishing RR-02, RR-03, and RR-04 footer codes.
Page-one report-detail identifiers are distinct from internal-header codes and already have their own same-message MODIFY.
Correcting internal-header codes does not change the variant set, selection basis, or exposure-level mapping.
The header-code correction does not modify the report's visual-quality standard, design direction, or cross-variant visual consistency.
Internal-header identifiers do not affect the customer-facing page-two copy governed by this Requirement.
The internal-page header's coverage, style, and information categories remain unchanged; the variant-specific code values are owned by the source code-consistency Requirement.
Internal-header code corrections do not change the front-page dashboard's fields, prominence, heading, or visibility.
The source decision changes displayed internal-header codes, not which customer fields are editable or how the assessment-date field behaves.
The general footer's style, page coverage, information categories, and warning coexistence remain unchanged; variant-specific footer codes are separately represented.
Header-code consistency does not alter the front-page explanation content, format, or detail level.
The internal-header correction does not change the final-page warning's presence, message, visual treatment, or footer relationship.
The vehicle-group display format and prohibition on checkbox presentation are unaffected by internal-header code corrections.
